summaryText:
Pastor Travis Hearn continued the series My Wounds Won't Win with week three, titled Hidden Wounds. He began by observing that many of us become skilled at hiding what we carry, covering disappointment with a smile, insecurity with confidence, and loneliness with busyness. Building on last week's message about not bleeding onto others, he emphasized that the greater tragedy is not being wounded, but hiding the wound or hiding from it. Nobody knowing we are hurting does not mean we are healed.

Teaching from Mark 5:24-34, Pastor Travis walked through the story of the woman who suffered with bleeding for twelve years. He explained that under the law in Leviticus she would have been considered ceremonially unclean, cut off from worship and community, so her deepest wound was isolation as much as illness. She spent all she had on doctors and only grew worse, which he connected to our tendency to try to fix hidden hurts with everything except Jesus.

The message had three main thoughts. First, hiding will only continue to hurt us. Pastor Travis tied this to James 5:16, noting that honesty comes before healing and that pain kept in isolation grows rather than fades. Second, Jesus is not afraid of what we are hiding. The woman touched Jesus, and instead of making him unclean, he made her clean. Jesus asked who had touched him in order to bring her out of hiding, and she told him the whole truth. He called her "daughter," restoring her identity and belonging as well as her body. Pastor Travis taught that Jesus never calls people by their wounds, but by the truth of who they are. Third, we should not let anything keep us from pursuing Jesus. The woman pressed through a crowd and through her own fear and shame, and Pastor Travis taught that healing begins when our direction changes, not when our circumstances do. He invited listeners to name the crowd standing between them and Jesus, such as fear, failure, unforgiveness, offense, disappointment, or addiction, and to press toward him, remembering the invitation of Matthew 11:28-30 to come to Jesus and find rest.

The service closed with an invitation for anyone who wanted to begin following Jesus to pray and give their life to him, and with a reminder that a wound that has been hidden does not have to stay unhealed. Pastor Travis also encouraged the church to join the Wednesday night midweek gathering and to share the series with others.
mainPoints: Hiding our wounds only prolongs the hurt; healing begins where hiding ends, through honesty with God and trusted believers.
Jesus is not afraid of what we are hiding. He cleanses, calls us by our true identity as his sons and daughters, and restores us fully.
Do not let fear, shame, or any crowd keep you from pursuing Jesus; healing begins when our direction changes and we press toward him.

versesMentioned.text: As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.

So Jesus went with him. A large crowd followed and pressed around him. And a woman was there who had been subject to bleeding for twelve years. She had suffered a great deal under the care of many doctors and had spent all she had, yet instead of getting better she grew worse. When she heard about Jesus, she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his cloak, because she thought, "If I just touch his clothes, I will be healed." Immediately her bleeding stopped and she felt in her body that she was freed from her suffering. At once Jesus realized that power had gone out from him. He turned around in the crowd and asked, "Who touched my clothes?" "You see the people crowding against you," his disciples answered, "and yet you can ask, 'Who touched me?'" But Jesus kept looking around to see who had done it. Then the woman, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell at his feet and, trembling with fear, told him the whole truth. He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace and be freed from your suffering."
Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective.

Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy and my burden is light.

Monday.scripture: James 5:16: "Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed."
Monday.action: Take five quiet minutes to write down one hurt, worry, or struggle you have been hiding. Then consider one trusted believer you could share it with this week.
Monday.prayer: Lord, thank you that you want to heal me, not embarrass me. Give me courage to stop hiding and to be honest with you and with others. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Mark 5:26: "She had suffered a great deal under the care of many doctors and had spent all she had, yet instead of getting better she grew worse."
Tuesday.focus: Bring Jesus the places we keep trying to fix on our own.
Tuesday.action: Name one thing you turn to (busyness, achievement, distraction) to avoid a hidden hurt. Pause for a few minutes today and bring that exact place to Jesus in prayer.
Tuesday.prayer: Jesus, I confess that I have tried to fix things in my own strength. Today I bring you the places I have kept to myself. Please heal what only you can touch. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Mark 5:33: "Then the woman, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell at his feet and, trembling with fear, told him the whole truth."
Wednesday.focus: Tell God the whole truth, not the edited version.
Wednesday.action: Spend time in prayer telling God the full, unfiltered truth about how you are really doing. If you are able, join a midweek service, Bible study, or time of fellowship with other believers tonight.
Wednesday.prayer: Father, you already know everything and you love me anyway. Help me to speak the whole truth to you and to receive your love. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Mark 5:34: "He said to her, 'Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace and be freed from your suffering.'"
Thursday.focus: Jesus names us by who we are in him, not by our wounds.
Thursday.action: Write down one label your wound has given you. Next to it, write a truth God says about you, such as beloved son or daughter. Read it aloud morning and evening.
Thursday.prayer: Jesus, thank you for calling me your own. Replace the labels I have believed with the truth of who I am in you. Amen.

Friday.scripture: Mark 5:27-28: "When she heard about Jesus, she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his cloak, because she thought, 'If I just touch his clothes, I will be healed.'"
Friday.focus: Press through whatever stands between you and Jesus.
Friday.action: Identify the crowd between you and Jesus (fear, shame, unforgiveness, disappointment). Take one small step toward him today, such as a prayer, a confession, or a moment of surrender.
Friday.prayer: Lord, I want to press toward you. Give me enough faith to take one step today, and help me not to let anything keep me from you. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: Matthew 11:28: "Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest."
Saturday.focus: Rest in Jesus and invite others to meet him.
Saturday.action: Set aside quiet time to rest in God's presence. Reflect on what he has shown you this week, and consider inviting someone to watch this series or join you at church next Sunday.
Saturday.prayer: Jesus, thank you for inviting the weary to come to you. Give my soul rest, keep healing what I have hidden, and help me care for others who may be carrying hidden wounds. Amen.

title: How to Heal the Wounds You Keep Hiding | Hidden Wounds
